Use `snl init` only when the target directory is intended to become a new SNL workspace.

### Command path
`init` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The shell adapter is `snl init`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"init","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"force": false}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. The root path is the target. No implicit parent-directory search is allowed.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"init","data":...,"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains the initialized workspace version, canonical root, and created paths.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"init","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":...,"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Mutating. It must refuse a non-empty or already initialized target unless an explicitly specified, separately validated recovery mode exists; publication is all-or-nothing. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.
